Multiprogramming & Multitasking OS
Multiprogramming
Multiple programs kept in memory.
CPU switches when one process waits for I/O.
Improves CPU utilization.

Multitasking
Extension of multiprogramming.
Multiple tasks run apparently simultaneously.
Uses context switching and time sharing.

Multiprocessing, Distributed OS & RTOS
Multiprocessing OS
Uses more than one CPU.
Improves reliability and throughput.

Distributed OS
Multiple interconnected computers share resources.

Real-Time OS (RTOS)
Ensures operations complete within strict time limits.
Used in robotics and air traffic control systems.

Bootloader Process
BIOS loads the bootloader from the storage device.
Bootloader loads the Operating System kernel.
After kernel loads, the OS starts user-space programs.
Examples: GRUB (Linux), Bootmgr (Windows), boot.efi (MacOS).

32-bit vs 64-bit Operating System
Feature | 32-bit OS | 64-bit OS
Memory Addressing | 2^32 addresses (~4GB RAM) | 2^64 addresses (very large memory)
Register Size | 32-bit registers | 64-bit registers
Data Processing | Processes 4 bytes per cycle | Processes 8 bytes per cycle
Compatibility | Runs only 32-bit OS | Can run both 32-bit and 64-bit OS

First Come, First Serve
(FCFS)
FCFS is a non-preemptive scheduling algorithm where the process that
arrives first in the ready queue is executed first.
Simple Execution
Processes are served in the order they arrive.
Convoy Effect
A long burst time process can significantly increase the average wait
time for subsequent shorter processes, leading to poor resource
management.

Multi-Level Queue (MLQ)
MLQ divides the ready queue into
multiple sub-queues based on process
properties like priority or type. Each
queue has its own scheduling algorithm.
Fixed Assignment
Processes are permanently assigned to a queue.
Queue-Specific Algorithms
Example: System processes (SP) use RR, Interactive
processes (IP) use RR, Batch processes (BP) use FCFS.
Fixed Priority Preemptive
Scheduling among queues is fixed-priority preemptive
(e.g., foreground has absolute priority over background).
Starvation & Convoy Effect
Lower priority processes can starve, and the convoy effect
is present.
